about.title: Personal Injury Help in Merced, California
about.longDescription: Getting hurt in Merced can turn an ordinary week upside down. One minute you are heading down G Street or R Street; the next you are dealing with a tow truck, an emergency room bill, and an insurance adjuster who wants a recorded statement. In 2025, Merced recorded 246 injury collisions. Those crashes left 349 people injured and took 3 lives in a city of roughly 82,000 residents. Public collision records show the heaviest counts along G Street, R Street, M Street, and W 16th Street, and reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. We are here to make the next step simpler. Our team handles personal injury claims in Merced County. We review your situation at no charge and, if you decide to move forward, work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless your case ends in a recovery. Whether you were hurt behind the wheel, on a bicycle, on foot, or on someone else's property, California's deadlines are real: most claims must be filed within two years, and claims against a public agency can carry a window as short as six months.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Merced Claim

items.title: Two years, sometimes six months
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county, or state agency may need to be filed within six months. Knowing which clock applies to you matters from day one.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly responsible reduces what you can recover but does not eliminate it. An adjuster who says otherwise is not giving you the full picture.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California does not place a ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life, or emotional distress. Your losses are evaluated on their own terms.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: Our team is paid only if your case results in a recovery. If nothing is recovered, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: Where do injury crashes tend to happen in Merced?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, the highest volumes in Merced fall along G Street, R Street, M Street, and W 16th Street. These are simply the corridors where the most reported collisions occur, not a judgment about any road itself. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Merced County?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a public roadway defect, a claim may need to be filed within six months. Our team can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the other driver says I caused part of the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. That means your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility, but you are not barred from recovering simply because you were partly at fault. How fault is assigned is often disputed, which is one reason an independent review is worthwhile.
